questions.q: For luxury kitchen sinks, which grade of stainless steel is most common?
o: SS 430
SS 304 or SS 316.
SS 202
SS 410
questions.n: These austenitic grades contain high nickel and chromium, making them the standard for high-end, corrosion-resistant kitchen sinks.

questions.q: What is a "P-trap" used for?
o: To increase the velocity of the water as it exits the fixture.
To filter out solid waste before it enters the main sewer line.
To provide a water seal that prevents sewer gases from entering the building.
To allow for easy disconnection of the sink from the wall.
questions.n: The dip in the pipe holds a 'trap seal' of water that acts as a barrier against toxic and foul-smelling gases.

questions.q: What is a "Cleanout" in a plumbing system?
o: An access point in the drainage system used for clearing clogs.
A chemical used to dissolve hair and grease in the pipes.
The final stage of a wastewater treatment plant.
A valve used to flush out sediment from a water heater.
questions.n: Cleanouts are capped openings that allow plumbing snakes or rods to enter the system to remove obstructions.

questions.q: What is "Water Hammer"?
o: A tool used to drive copper pipes into tight wall cavities.
The sound of water dripping into a metallic basin.
The noise and vibration caused by a sudden stop in water flow, usually fixed with an air chamber.
The pressure used to test the integrity of new pipes.
questions.n: When a valve closes quickly, the momentum of the water creates a shockwave that rattles the pipes.

questions.q: Which valve is commonly used at the base of a pump suction pipe to maintain "prime"?
o: Gate Valve
Angle Valve
Foot Valve.
Globe Valve
questions.n: A foot valve is a type of check valve that keeps the pump suction line full of water to prevent air locks.

questions.q: What is a "Sump Pump" used for?
o: To circulate hot water throughout a building.
To inject chlorine into a swimming pool system.
To increase the water pressure in high-rise showers.
To pump out water that has accumulated in a basement or pit below the sewer level.
questions.n: When gravity drainage is impossible, a sump pump lifts water up to the level of the main sewer line.

questions.q: In plumbing, what does "Fixture Unit" (FU) measure?
o: The probable discharge into the drainage system by various types of plumbing fixtures.
The total number of sinks in a building.
The weight of a porcelain toilet.
The time it takes for a bathtub to drain completely.
questions.n: It is a mathematical factor used to size pipes based on the frequency and volume of use.

questions.q: What is a "Backflow Preventer"?
o: A device that prevents sewage from overflowing into the street.
A trap used to keep hair from entering the drain.
A pump that reverses the direction of water flow.
A device that prevents contaminated water from flowing back into the clean water supply.
questions.n: It protects the potable water system from cross-contamination due to pressure changes.

questions.q: What is "Greywater"?
o: Industrial chemicals used in masonry cleaning.
Water that contains toilet waste.
Rainwater collected from the roof.
Wastewater from sinks, showers, and laundry that does not contain human waste.
questions.n: Greywater is relatively clean compared to blackwater and can often be recycled for irrigation.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a "Vent Stack"?
o: To drain water from the upper floors.
To store excess water during peak usage times.
To allow air into the plumbing system to equalize pressure and protect trap seals.
To serve as an emergency exit for fire gases.
questions.n: Air prevents the vacuum effect that would otherwise 'siphon' water out of the P-traps.

questions.q: Which grade of stainless steel is most resistant to corrosion and often used in marine or kitchen environments?
o: SS 201
SS 304
SS 409
questions.n: The addition of molybdenum makes SS 316 the 'marine grade' standard for the most demanding environments.

questions.q: Which stainless steel finish is characterized by a "brushed" look with fine parallel lines?
o: Sandblasted Finish
Hairline Finish.
Matte Finish
Mirror Finish
questions.n: Hairline finish uses continuous abrasives to create long, fine, parallel grain lines.

questions.q: Which is NOT a finish of stainless steel but rather a sheen level of paint?
o: Gloss / Semi-gloss.
BA (Bright Annealed)
No. 4 Brush
2B (Cold Rolled)
questions.n: While metals have reflectivity, 'Gloss' and 'Semi-gloss' are terms primarily used to define paint sheens.

questions.q: What do you call the long-span steel structure consisting of interconnected triangles?
o: Rigid Frame
Portal Frame
Steel Joist
Steel Truss.
questions.n: Trusses use the inherent stability of triangles to span long distances with minimal material.

questions.q: What is a "Space Frame"?
o: A 3D truss-like structure used to cover large areas without interior columns.
A frame used to hold satellites in space.
The structural skeleton of a glass skyscraper.
A hollow steel column used for elevators.
questions.n: Space frames use a multidirectional grid of struts to distribute loads in three dimensions.

questions.q: Which steel gauge is commonly used for handrails to balance weight and strength?
o: 5.0mm to 10.0mm
0.5mm to 0.8mm
1.5mm to 2.0mm (Schedule 40 is common for heavy-duty).
0.1mm
questions.n: This range provides the necessary wall thickness to resist bending and support user weight.

questions.q: What is "Galvanizing"?
o: Mixing steel with carbon to make it harder.
Painting steel with a metallic-colored finish.
The process of coating steel with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting.
Heating steel and then cooling it in oil.
questions.n: The zinc acts as a sacrificial anode that corrodes instead of the underlying steel.

questions.q: What do you call the steel cladding material often used for modern building facades?
o: Vinyl Siding
Plywood
Drywall
Aluminum Composite Panel (ACP) or Metal Spandrel.
questions.n: These lightweight panels provide a sleek, durable exterior finish for modern structures.

questions.q: What is "I-Beam" (H-Beam) primarily used for?
o: As a major horizontal load-bearing member (Beam).
To reinforce the edges of a concrete slab.
As a vertical support in a wall.
As a decorative trim around windows.
questions.n: The I-shape is optimized for resisting bending (flexure) along its length.

questions.q: What is a "Purlin"?
o: A vertical post that supports a fence.
A horizontal structural member in a roof that supports the roofing sheets.
The main drain pipe in a plumbing system.
A type of decorative molding for ceilings.
questions.n: Purlins span between trusses or rafters to provide the direct support for the metal roofing.

questions.q: Which steel finish is "Satin"?
o: A smooth, low-luster finish between matte and gloss.
A rough, textured finish like sandpaper.
A transparent finish that shows the metal's grain clearly.
A finish that looks like rusted iron.
questions.n: It provides a soft sheen that is not as sharp as a mirror finish but more refined than matte.

questions.q: What is "Cor-Ten" steel?
o: A type of lightweight steel used for aircraft.
Steel that has been coated in a plastic polymer.
Weathering steel designed to form a stable rust-like appearance to resist further corrosion.
A brand of high-strength structural bolts.
questions.n: It eliminates the need for painting by forming a protective layer of oxidation.

questions.q: What is a "Shear Stud" in composite construction?
o: A decorative stud used on leather upholstery.
A steel pin welded to a beam that connects it to a concrete slab, ensuring they act as one unit.
A bolt used to connect two wooden beams.
A nail used for light-gauge steel framing.
questions.n: They transfer shear forces between the steel and concrete to create a composite beam.

questions.q: Why is SS 202 rarely used for outdoor handrails near the sea?
o: It has lower nickel content and is much more prone to "tea-staining" or rusting.
It cannot be welded with standard equipment.
It is too expensive compared to other grades.
It is too heavy to be supported by standard walls.
questions.n: The low nickel and high manganese content make it vulnerable to salt-air corrosion.

questions.q: What is "Light Gauge Steel" (LGS)?
o: A type of rebar with no ribs.
The steel used in the manufacturing of cars.
Steel that is light in color to reflect sunlight.
Cold-formed steel used for framing partitions and low-rise residential structures.
questions.n: LGS is a fast, versatile alternative to wood framing or CHB walls.

questions.q: What is the most expensive type of insulation commonly used for high-end acoustic treatment?
o: Recycled Paper (Cellulose)
Aerogel or specialized High-Density Mineral Wool.
Polystyrene (Styrofoam)
Glass Fiber (Fiberglass)
questions.n: These materials offer extreme performance in thin profiles but come at a premium cost.

questions.q: What is "Reverberation Time"?
o: The time it takes for a sound to travel across a room.
The time it takes for sound to "fade away" or decay by 60 decibels after the source has stopped.
The delay between a flash of lightning and a clap of thunder.
The length of time a speaker can talk before their voice gets tired.
questions.n: Known as RT60, it measures how 'live' or 'dead' a room feels.

questions.q: Which acoustic material is best for "absorbing" sound to prevent echoes in an auditorium?
o: Ceramic Tile
Plywood Sheets
Polished Granite
Acoustic Panels / Rockwool / Fiberglass.
questions.n: Porous materials trap sound energy and convert it into heat, reducing reflections.

questions.q: Which area of a theater typically requires the most acoustic absorption?
o: The Front Stage
The Floor
The Rear Wall (to prevent "slap-back" echoes).
The Entrance Doors
questions.n: Absorbing sound at the back prevents it from bouncing back to the stage and confusing the performers.

questions.q: What does NRC stand for in acoustics?
o: Natural Resonance Capacity
Noise Reduction Coefficient (measures how much sound a material absorbs).
National Radio Commission
New Room Classification
questions.n: NRC values range from 0 (total reflection) to 1 (total absorption).

questions.q: What is STC?
o: Structural Tension Capacity
Special Technical Committee
Sound Transmission Class (measures how well a wall/partition blocks sound from passing through).
Standard Theater Ceiling
questions.n: Higher STC ratings mean better privacy and soundproofing between rooms.

questions.q: How do you treat "Flanking Paths" in acoustics?
o: By painting the room a darker color.
By sealing gaps at the top and bottom of walls, and ensuring ducts/pipes are insulated.
By adding more speakers.
By opening all the windows.
questions.n: Flanking paths are 'leaks' where sound bypasses a primary barrier.

questions.q: Which material is known for being a "sound reflector"?
o: Marble / Concrete / Glass.
Carpeting
Open-cell Foam
Heavy Curtains
questions.n: Hard, dense, and non-porous surfaces reflect almost all sound waves that hit them.

questions.q: What is "Decibel" (dB) a measure of?
o: The pitch of a sound.
The speed of sound in water.
Sound intensity or loudness.
The weight of a speaker.
questions.n: The decibel is a logarithmic unit used to express the ratio of two values of a physical power.

questions.q: Why are "Bass Traps" placed in the corners of a recording studio?
o: To keep the corners of the room clean from dust.
To hide the electrical wiring.
Because low-frequency sound energy tends to build up in corners.
To make the room look larger.
questions.n: Corner placement allows the trap to absorb 'room modes' and standing waves effectively.

questions.q: What is "White Noise"?
o: A high-pitched alarm signal.
Silence in a vacuum.
A constant background sound used to mask distracting noises.
The sound of someone whispering.
questions.n: It contains all frequencies across the audible spectrum in equal measure.

questions.q: Which type of ceiling is best for acoustic flexibility?
o: Concrete Slab
Suspended Acoustic Ceiling (T-runner system).
Exposed Wood Beams
Plasterboard Ceiling
questions.n: Panels can be easily swapped or moved to adjust the room's NRC rating.

questions.q: What is "Sound Diffusion"?
o: Sucking all the sound out of a room.
Scattering sound waves to prevent hotspots and create a uniform sound field.
The amplification of sound using electronic speakers.
The process of sound traveling through a solid wall.
questions.n: Diffusers break up direct reflections to make a room sound 'larger' and more natural.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a "Floating Floor"?
o: To provide a storage space for cables underneath.
To prevent the house from sinking into soft soil.
To make the floor easier to clean.
To decouple the floor from the structure to prevent impact noise (e.g., footsteps) from traveling.
questions.n: The air gap or resilient layer stops vibration from moving into the building's skeleton.

questions.q: Which insulation material is also known for its high fire resistance?
o: Rockwool (Stone wool).
Bubble Wrap
Cork
Urethane Foam
questions.n: Made from volcanic rock, it can withstand temperatures over 1000°C.

questions.q: Which window hardware is used to allow a window to "swing" open like a door?
o: Sliding Track
Bolts
Casement Hinge.
Awning Stay
questions.n: A casement window is attached to its frame by one or more hinges at the side.

questions.q: What is a "Friction Stay"?
o: A device that prevents the window from being opened too far.
A type of hinge for awning or casement windows that holds the window open at a specific position without a separate stay.
A type of glue used to hold glass in place.
A metal rod used to lock a door from the inside.
questions.n: The internal friction of the hinge allows the window to remain open at any angle.

questions.q: Which door fitting is used for "Frameless Glass" doors to allow them to swing in both directions?
o: Spring Hinge
Floor Hinge (or Pivot Hinge).
Butt Hinge
Piano Hinge
questions.n: These are mounted in the floor and at the top of the door, allowing for a 180-degree double-action swing.

questions.q: What do you call the wall material made of wood fibers and plastic, often used for exterior decking or cladding?
o: Natural Teak
Hardiflex
MDF (Medium Density Fiberboard)
WPC (Wood Plastic Composite).
questions.n: WPC combines the appearance of wood with the durability and low maintenance of plastic.

questions.q: What is a "Thermal Break" in an aluminum window frame?
o: A gap used to allow for the expansion of the frame in summer.
The point at which the aluminum melts.
An insulating material placed between the inner and outer parts of the frame to prevent heat transfer.
A crack in the frame caused by extreme heat.
questions.n: Aluminum is a good conductor; the 'break' stops the flow of heat or cold through the frame.

questions.q: In NSCP, what is the "Basic Wind Speed" based on?
o: The speed of the fastest typhoon ever recorded.
The 3-second gust speed at 10 meters above ground for a specific return period.
The average wind speed over a whole year.
The speed at which a person can no longer stand upright.
questions.n: Structural design must account for the maximum sudden force a building will experience.

questions.q: What do you call the weight of the building's own structure and permanent equipment?
o: Dead Load.
Seismic Load
Live Load
Impact Load
questions.n: The dead load includes the weight of the columns, beams, slabs, and fixed partitions.

questions.q: What is a "Multipoint Lock"?
o: A locking system for doors or windows that bolts at multiple points along the frame for high security.
A lock used on a shared apartment door for multiple residents.
A lock that requires three different keys.
A lock that can only be opened from the outside.
questions.n: It distributes the locking force, making it much harder to pry open.

questions.q: Which is a "not-finish" of steel but a type of protective coating?
o: Brushed Finish
Bituminous Coating (used for underground steel).
Anodized Finish
Powder Coating
questions.n: This thick, tar-like substance is a protective barrier, not an architectural 'finish'.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a "Header" in a door or window opening?
o: To serve as a place to hang a sign.
To act as a decorative 'eyebrow' over the window.
To support the structural load above the opening and transfer it to the side studs.
To provide a mounting point for the door closer.
questions.n: Without a header, the weight of the wall or roof would crush the window or door frame.
